t: There is no house here now, but this was the site of Beaufort House, a grand mansion beside the Thames. Thomas More built it around 1520, while he was Lord Chancellor to Henry VIII. When he was arrested in 1534, all his property was forfeited to the Crown. Later owners included William Cecil, Robert Cecil, the Duke of Buckingham and Sir Hans Sloane, whose collection became the foundation of the British Museum. The house took the name Beaufort in 1682, from the 1st Duke of Beaufort. It was demolished in 1739, and it gave its name to Beaufort Street.
